# `set_focuser_value`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Set a focuser control value (backlash or step-register reset).

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build differs for backlash only, where it can persist the value (READ)) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xe7e10, SetValue @0x15c660 (64-bit build); SetValue @0xdef24 (32-bit build, nonzero backend result maps to 300); eaf_set_backlash is a function pointer set by eaf_open; dw9800 backend @0x2f3010 returns 10, default backend @0x2f17bc writes "backlash" via set_conf_int (0 ok, 2 write failed, 5 not open); tier INFERRED |

Requires an open focuser. reset_step converts the requested UI step with the cached scaling, writes the hardware position register (eaf_set_position) and updates the cached logical position, hardware position and remainder; this resets the position counter and is not demonstrated motor travel. backlash calls the focuser backlash setter, which in the 64-bit build is a stub that always fails, so an open focuser always replies 300 for backlash there. In the 32-bit build the backend is chosen when the focuser is opened. One backend is a stub that also fails (300), the other stores the backlash value in the device configuration and succeeds when the focuser is open, so there backlash can succeed and persist (READ). max_step has no setter (210). No rollback and no wait.

Side effects: reset_step rewrites the focuser position register and cached position state; a failed backlash call only writes diagnostic log state.

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"set_focuser_value"`. [READ] |
| `params` | any | yes | - | Object form {name, val} or positional array [name, val]; both members required, no defaults. A scalar, missing or empty params gives 105. name matching is a case-insensitive substring search within max_step, backlash, reset_step (first match wins). [READ] |

Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). ## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 105 | name missing or not a string (including scalar or empty params) | `expected string param` |
| 104 | val missing or not an integer or boolean | `expected int param` |
| 109 | name matches none of the control names | `unexpected param` |
| 318 | Recognised control but the focuser is not open | `device not connected` |
| 210 | max_step setter requested (unsupported) | `not supported` |
| 300 | Driver set call fails (always for backlash in the 64-bit build) or reset scaling maxima are not positive | `internal error` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

## Example

Request, request:

```json
{"id":17,"method":"set_focuser_value","params":{"name":"reset_step","val":1200}}
```

Request, positional - Positional form:

```json
{"id":18,"method":"set_focuser_value","params":["reset_step",1200]}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_focuser_value","result":0,"code":0,"id":17}
```

Reply, backlash-fails - Backlash on an open focuser (64-bit build):

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_focuser_value","error":"internal error","code":300,"id":19}
```
